content:
Laredo Fire Chief Guillermo Heard laid out the state of the city's fire department — from staffing and rising equipment costs to the October DoubleTree fire and a new push for firefighter wellness — in a talk to the Laredo Gateway Rotary on Nov. 2, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The department has 15 fire stations and aims for a three- to five-minute response time, Heard said. It is authorized for 469 firefighters and has more than 420 on staff. Staffing fell after retirements, pension-system changes and COVID-19, and the chief said he moved administrative personnel into line positions to fill gaps.

Equipment costs have climbed sharply, according to Heard: a fire truck that cost about $500,000 before COVID now costs about $1 million, and ladder trucks cost more. The department answers about 30,000 to 35,000 calls a year, mostly for emergency medical service, driven by an aging population and limited health-care access, with the busiest ambulance areas in south Laredo. Two new stations are being built, one near the Buena Vista station and one near the Unitec area, and each takes about one to one and a half years to build once started.

Heard called the DoubleTree fire one of the department's largest fires in 30 years. The call came in about 12:52 a.m. on Oct. 7, with the fifth floor on fire, and about 80 firefighters responded. More than 120 people were in the hotel, mostly National Guard personnel. There were no deaths and no serious injuries: four people were taken to a hospital for smoke inhalation and released, and four others drove themselves to care and were released.

Crews withdrew from the sixth floor after it felt spongy and exposed steel beams and columns were seen, and drones helped assess the damage, Heard said. The hotel remains an active scene with a collapse zone and a fire watch while the owner's structural engineering firm stabilizes it. The investigation, involving the Laredo Fire Department, the Texas State Fire Marshal's Office and the ATF, cannot fully proceed until stabilization is done, and the sprinkler system is under investigation.

"I'm very proud of the work we did. Nobody died. Nobody got seriously hurt," Heard said of the response.

On wellness, Heard said the department hired a psychologist specializing in firefighters, offers regular counseling and a peer-support team, and opened a wellness facility in a former fire station on Del Mar Boulevard, with offices for the psychologist and a chaplain, a conference room, a decompression room and a gym. The effort was prompted in part by a firefighter suicide in August.

Source: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 17, 2026.

title: Laredo Fire Chief Talks Staffing, DoubleTree Fire and Firefighter Wellness
